# WTR Android - LLM Codebase Guide

This file explains the WTR Android codebase for AI coding assistants and future maintainers.

## Project summary

WTR Android is a Flutter app for reading and discovering content from WTR and future extension-based sources. The long-term goal is to support multiple content types through one common source interface:

- Novels
- Manga
- Anime
- Future custom extensions

The app should remain source-agnostic. UI screens should call a shared source interface instead of directly depending on one API.

## Tech stack

- Flutter
- Dart
- Dio
- HTTP
- SharedPreferences
- AdaptiveTheme
- Responsive Framework
- Google Nav Bar
- Logger
- DNS Client
- Cloudflare bypass/interceptor packages
- Dart web scraper

## Current entry points

- `lib/main.dart`
  - Initializes Flutter bindings.
  - Runs `WtrApp`.

- `lib/src/app.dart`
  - Defines `WtrApp`.
  - Configures `AdaptiveTheme`.
  - Configures responsive breakpoints.
  - Shows splash screen before loading Home.

## Current important files

- `lib/src/core/constants/api_constants.dart`
  - Contains current WTR API base URLs and paths.

- `lib/src/core/network/dio_client.dart`
  - Central Dio client.
  - Adds logging interceptors.
  - Contains proxy POST helper.

- `lib/src/features/home/presentation/home_page.dart`
  - Current main screen.
  - Uses Google Nav Bar.
  - Currently has Home and Search tabs.

- `lib/src/features/home/data/home_repository.dart`
  - Fetches current WTR home/ranking data.
  - Falls back to demo data on errors.

## Desired architecture

The project should move toward this structure:

```txt
lib/src/
├── core/
│   ├── constants/
│   ├── network/
│   ├── storage/
│   └── utils/
├── extensions/
│   ├── models/
│   │   ├── content_item.dart
│   │   ├── content_details.dart
│   │   ├── chapter_item.dart
│   │   └── content_source.dart
│   ├── registry/
│   │   └── source_registry.dart
│   ├── novel/
│   │   └── wtr_novel_source.dart
│   ├── manga/
│   │   └── manga_source.dart
│   └── anime/
│       └── anime_source.dart
├── features/
│   ├── home/
│   ├── search/
│   ├── details/
│   ├── chapter_list/
│   ├── reader/
│   ├── extensions/
│   └── settings/
└── app.dart
```

## Core design rule

Do not put source-specific API logic directly inside UI screens.

Bad:

```dart
HomePage -> directly calls WTR endpoint
```

Good:

```dart
HomePage -> activeSource.getHome()
```

## Planned common interface

```dart
abstract class ContentSource {
  String get id;
  String get name;
  String get type;
  String get baseUrl;

  Future<List<ContentItem>> getHome();
  Future<List<ContentItem>> search(String query);
  Future<ContentDetails> getDetails(String id);
  Future<List<ChapterItem>> getChapters(String id);
}
```

## Planned common models

### ContentItem

Represents a generic item shown in Home/Search.

Suggested fields:

- `id`
- `title`
- `imageUrl`
- `subtitle`
- `type`
- `sourceId`
- `extra`

### ContentDetails

Represents details page data.

Suggested fields:

- `id`
- `title`
- `imageUrl`
- `description`
- `author`
- `status`
- `genres`
- `type`
- `sourceId`
- `extra`

### ChapterItem

Represents novel chapters, manga chapters, or anime episodes.

Suggested fields:

- `id`
- `title`
- `number`
- `url`
- `type`
- `sourceId`
- `extra`

## Source registry

Create a registry that stores all available sources.

Expected behavior:

- Return all sources.
- Return source by ID.
- Return default source.
- Load selected source ID from preferences.
- Save selected source ID to preferences.

## Settings feature

Settings should eventually include:

- Theme mode: light/dark/system
- DNS resolver selection/test
- GitHub link
- Issue report link
- Contact link
- About app
- App version/developer info

## DNS resolver feature

DNS resolver logic should live in:

```txt
lib/src/core/network/dns_resolver_service.dart
```

It should not be mixed with UI code.

Settings UI should only call service methods.

## Networking rules

- Use `DioClient` for API requests.
- Add source-specific headers inside source classes or source config.
- Log requests and parser errors using `Logger`.
- Keep Cloudflare-specific logic isolated.
- Keep scraping logic isolated inside extension/source classes.

## UI rules

- Home should display `ContentItem` objects.
- Search should display `ContentItem` objects.
- Details should display `ContentDetails`.
- ChapterList should display `ChapterItem` objects.
- Reader/Player should branch by content type only at the final rendering layer.

## Navigation plan

Main bottom tabs:

```txt
Home
Search
Extensions
Settings
```

Details and Reader/Player should be pushed screens, not bottom tabs.

## Extension behavior

When user selects an extension:

1. Save selected source ID in SharedPreferences.
2. Update active source in app state.
3. Home refreshes using selected source.
4. Search uses selected source.
5. Details and ChapterList use selected source.

## Current API notes

Current WTR API paths:

```dart
webBaseUrl = 'https://wtr-lab.com'
apiProxyBaseUrl = 'https://cors-bypasser-pro.vercel.app/proxy?url=https://wtr-lab.com'
serieRanking = '/api/serie/ranking'
search = '/api/search'
novelDetails = '/api/novel/details'
chapterList = '/api/novel/chapters'
readerGet = '/api/reader/get'
```

## Development order recommendation

1. Add common models.
2. Add `ContentSource` interface.
3. Convert current WTR novel API into `WtrNovelSource`.
4. Add `SourceRegistry`.
5. Add `PrefsService`.
6. Update Home to use active source.
7. Update Search to use active source.
8. Update Details and ChapterList to use active source.
9. Add Extensions tab.
10. Add Settings tab.
11. Add DNS resolver service.
12. Add manga source.
13. Add anime source.
14. Add reader/player type-specific rendering.

## Important constraints for AI assistants

- Do not rewrite the whole app unless explicitly asked.
- Provide complete file contents when modifying code.
- Always mention the exact file path.
- Keep code Flutter/Dart compatible with SDK `>=3.4.0 <4.0.0`.
- Keep imports clean and relative to the current project style.
- Prefer simple working code over over-engineered architecture.
- Preserve existing working UI while migrating gradually.
- Do not remove demo fallback behavior unless asked.
- Do not hardcode new APIs into UI screens.
- Do not expose secrets, tokens, private keys, or hidden credentials.
